items.item_text: Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.
Bachelor's degree in a related field and/or equivalent education, training, or experience.
Five (5) or more years of relevant experience, including volunteer coordination, human resources, program coordination, or managing large groups of individuals through multistep processes.
Two to five (2–5) years of supervisory or team leadership experience.

Demonstrated creativity, problem-solving skills, and initiative in identifying opportunities for improvement and implementing innovative solutions to enhance programs, processes, and participant experiences.
Experience working in a complex healthcare environment.
Experience coordinating volunteer programs involving diverse populations and multidisciplinary teams.
Experience developing or expanding volunteer programs and engagement initiatives.

Reporting to the Director of Experience Operations, the Volunteer Coordinator provides operational and functional oversight of volunteer recruitment, screening, onboarding, orientation, training, engagement, and retention across UC San Diego Health.

The Coordinator serves as a primary liaison for volunteers, staff, patients, and community members, building positive relationships with individuals of diverse ages, backgrounds, personalities, and professional roles.

This position is responsible for ensuring volunteer training and compliance, maintaining an active presence through regular volunteer rounding, and identifying creative and innovative opportunities to enhance programming and the volunteer experience.

The ideal candidate demonstrates strong interpersonal skills, initiative, sound judgment, and the ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with the Volunteer Services team and departmental stakeholders.
The Department of Volunteer Services is part of the Office of Experience Transformation at UC San Diego Health.
Volunteer Program Operations
Coordinate volunteer recruitment, interviewing, screening, onboarding, orientation, training, and retention.
Maintain accurate volunteer records, monitor training and compliance requirements, track participation, and generate reports using the volunteer database.
Manage daily volunteer operations, prioritize competing responsibilities, and coordinate special programs and initiatives.
Volunteer Engagement and Relationship Building
Build and maintain positive relationships with volunteers of diverse ages, backgrounds, and personalities, as well as healthcare professionals, departmental leaders, and community partners.

Conduct regular rounding with volunteers across UC San Diego Health to strengthen relationships, recognize contributions, address concerns, and identify opportunities to improve the volunteer experience.

Foster a welcoming and supportive environment by serving as a primary point of contact, maintaining regular communication, and promoting volunteer engagement and retention.Program Development and Innovation
Identify, develop, and implement creative and innovative approaches to enhance volunteer programming, engagement, and retention.
Collaborate with departmental stakeholders to develop new volunteer opportunities that support operational needs and enhance the patient, visitor, and team member experience.
Evaluate program effectiveness, measure impact, and implement improvements that support program growth.
Promote the volunteer program throughout UC San Diego Health and the Greater San Diego community.
Collaboration and Independent Decision-Making '
Work independently, demonstrate sound judgment, and take initiative to manage responsibilities, resolve challenges, and respond to changing priorities.
Collaborate with the Director, Volunteer Services team, and departmental stakeholders through open communication, shared problem-solving, and a team-oriented approach to achieving program goals.
Demonstrated knowledge of volunteer program operations, management, and industry best practices.

Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to build positive relationships and effectively engage with individuals of diverse ages, backgrounds, personalities, and professional roles.
Demonstrated ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, take initiative, and collaborate effectively with internal and external stakeholders.
Ability to proactively engage with individuals, solicit feedback, address concerns, and navigate challenging interpersonal situations with professionalism, empathy, and adaptability.
Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, competing responsibilities, and changing operational needs.
